- Policy stance: Hawkish. The FOMC raised the funds rate to 2.25–2.5%, signaled ongoing hikes, and kept QT on track to ramp to $60B Treasuries/$35B MBS in September—tightening financial conditions.
- SLOOS overlay (July 2022): Banks on net tightened standards and terms for C&I loans across firm sizes, CRE, and most residential mortgage categories; increased loan spreads and collateral requirements; and tightened for credit cards and subprime auto. Banks cited a weaker economic outlook and liquidity concerns. Demand was mixed—stronger for C&I and HELOCs, weaker for CRE and some mortgages.
- Implication: The combination of policy tightening and bank credit tightening points to a more restrictive credit channel than the FOMC statement alone suggests, increasing downside risk for credit‑sensitive sectors. Stronger C&I demand offers only partial offset.
